examples.en: The player broke through the defense and scored a goal.

examples.ko: 우리 영화가 관객 천만 명을 돌파했어요.
examples.en: Our movie passed ten million viewers.
Let's get through this hard time together.
I pushed through the snowy road and barely arrived.

examples.ko: 이번 달 판매량이 목표를 돌파할 거예요.
examples.en: This month's sales will surpass the target.
I found a way to break through the crisis.

explain: 장애물이나 어려움을 뚫고 지나갈 때, 숫자가 기준을 넘을 때 둘 다 써요. '관객 천만 돌파', '인구 5천만 돌파'처럼 뉴스 제목에 자주 나와요. 그냥 넘는 것은 '넘다', 힘껏 뚫고 나아가는 느낌이면 '돌파하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used both for pushing through an obstacle and for a number passing a mark. News headlines often say '관객 천만 돌파' (passes ten million viewers). '넘다' is plain crossing; '돌파하다' has the feel of forcing your way through.

examples.en: We buried our pet dog on the hill behind the house.
There are places that bury garbage in the ground.
In the old days, kings were buried in the mountains.
You have to bury it deep so it doesn't smell.
I want to bury the secret forever.
They kept records even when burying relics.

explain: 땅속에 묻을 때 써요. 장례에서 시신을 땅에 묻는 것을 말하기도 하는데, 대화에서는 '묻다'가 훨씬 쉽고 흔해요. '화장하다'(태우다)와 반대되는 방식이에요. '사회에서 매장되다'처럼 완전히 밀려나는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: Burying something in the ground, including burying a body at a funeral, although in conversation '묻다' is far easier and more common. The contrast is '화장하다' (cremate). It is also used figuratively for being shut out for good, as in '사회에서 매장되다'.

p.n: 매몰하다 is not used for burying a person's body.

en: doing; handiwork (usually of a bad deed)

examples.ko: 창문을 깬 건 옆집 아이들의 소행이에요.
examples.en: The kids next door are the ones who broke the window.
It hasn't been found out yet who did it.

examples.ko: 경찰은 이번 사건이 같은 사람의 소행이라고 봐요.
examples.en: The police think this incident is the work of the same person.

examples.ko: 이런 장난은 분명히 동생의 소행일 거예요.
examples.en: A prank like this must be my younger brother's doing.

examples.ko: 그의 소행을 알고 나서 모두 화가 났어요.
examples.en: Everyone got angry after learning what he had done.
The fire turned out to be the work of an arsonist.

explain: '누구의 소행'처럼 잘못되거나 나쁜 일을 한 사람을 말할 때 써요. 좋은 일에는 잘 안 쓰고, 그럴 때는 '행동'이나 '덕분'을 써요. 보통 '~의 소행이다' 꼴로 나와요.
explain_en: It is used to name who did something bad or wrong, almost always in the pattern '~의 소행이다'. For good deeds people say 행동 or 덕분 instead.

examples.en: In photography, capturing the moment matters most.
The suspect was caught on CCTV.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 인물의 감정 포착이 뛰어나요.
examples.en: This film is excellent at capturing characters' emotions.
We noticed the change late, so our response was late too.

examples.ko: 포착한 장면을 바로 올리지 말고 확인부터 하세요.
examples.en: Don't post the scene you captured right away; check it first.

examples.ko: 새 유행을 빠르게 포착하는 눈이 필요해요.
examples.en: You need an eye that quickly picks up on new trends.

explain: 순간, 낌새, 움직임처럼 놓치기 쉬운 것을 잡아낼 때 써요. 대개 '포착하다', '포착되다'로 쓰고, 뉴스에서 '카메라에 포착됐다'처럼 자주 나와요. 물건을 손으로 잡는 건 '잡다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it for catching something easy to miss, like a moment, a sign, or a movement. It is mostly used as 포착하다 or 포착되다, and news often says '카메라에 포착됐다'. For grabbing an object by hand, use 잡다.

examples.en: The sugar content of this snack is high.

examples.ko: 제품에 적힌 나트륨 함유량을 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check the sodium content written on the product.
The content differs a little from product to product.
The price differs depending on the vitamin content.

examples.ko: 이 물은 미네랄 함유량이 어느 정도예요?
examples.en: How much mineral content does this water have?
I bought a low-salt soy sauce with reduced content.

explain: 보통 '설탕 함유량', '나트륨 함유량'처럼 앞에 성분 이름을 붙여 써요. 포장지나 뉴스, 건강 이야기에서 자주 보여요. '함유량이 높다/낮다/많다/적다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is usually used with an ingredient in front, as in '설탕 함유량' or '나트륨 함유량'. You often see it on packaging, in the news and in health talk. Say '함유량이 높다/낮다/많다/적다'.

examples.ko: 그는 사기 행각이 들통나서 경찰에 잡혔어요.
examples.en: His fraud was exposed and he was caught by the police.

examples.ko: 범인은 해외에서 도피 행각을 벌이다 붙잡혔어요.
examples.en: The culprit was caught while on the run abroad.

examples.ko: 그 업체의 불법 행각은 뉴스에도 나왔어요.
examples.en: That company's illegal conduct was even on the news.

examples.ko: 이 행각에 속은 사람이 수백 명이에요.
examples.en: Hundreds of people were fooled by this scheme.
His suspicious behavior made the neighbors suspicious.
Every single thing he did was a lie.

explain: '사기 행각', '도피 행각', '불법 행각'처럼 나쁜 일이나 눈살 찌푸려지는 행동을 가리킬 때 써요. 좋은 일에는 쓰지 않아서 '행동'과 바꿔 쓰기 어려워요. 주로 뉴스나 글에서 많이 봐요.
explain_en: It is used for bad or objectionable behavior, as in '사기 행각' (fraud), '도피 행각' (life on the run) and '불법 행각' (illegal conduct). It is not used for good deeds, so it cannot simply replace '행동'. You see it mostly in news and writing.
